key_insight: Scalable DMD identifies coherent front-wing flow structures and their temporal dynamics while compressing approximately 6 TB of snapshots into 200 GB of modal data.
engineering_relevance: The method can help aerodynamicists interpret unsteady vortex behavior and reduce storage demands for high-fidelity motorsport simulations.
method: Simulate the Imperial Front Wing at Re = 2.2 × 10^5 using spectral/hp-element LES in Nektar++.
Apply scalable POD and DMD through the open-source pyLOM framework.
Associate DMD frequencies with flow mechanisms using point-probe spectra.
evidence_signal: The 49.72-million-degree-of-freedom simulation shows force-coefficient differences of 2.24% in lift and 2.87% in drag versus reference data; DMD modes at chord-based Strouhal numbers 5.1, 7.5 and 9.3 are associated with separation-bubble dynamics, canard vortex pulsation and endplate vortex meander.
watch_item: Demonstrated on one front-wing benchmark at one Reynolds number, the modal associations and compression performance require validation for other configurations.
paper_title: Scalable Modal Analysis of the Imperial Front Wing Flow Field
